title: arngz apply counts a fixed-size window that reached its origin as failed, and no apply has ever exited 0
body:
## What

hv, 10 Nov 2026, in a message hv typed into gtools-vc's window by mistake and gtools-vc handed to utilz-vc over the socket, received by vc's date -u of 06:02Z. hv's words, verbatim:

```text
I think there's some kind of bug with arngz that I can't identitfy. The issue I
have is with arngz which seems to be borking and exiting with "exit code 2" or
"exit code 1" depending on where I am. We need to have a look at the logs and
work out what is going wrong there (if anything), but I suspect an exit code
other than 0 means something isn't doing what it is supposed to.
```

hv's three screenshots are named in the handover, `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-vc/arngz-handover-20261110.md` (sha256 c0727ec6708e3f1dee92968a470a441b89e6c4570de555a7c46c4da9d99426b8, 130 lines, banked by vc from gtools-vc's scratch and byte-identical to it), whose analysis utilz-vc re-derived from the log and the source first-hand before filing.

utilz 2.14.8 from Homebrew (tag f2021ddc, installed 2026-10-30 21:51Z) with arngz 1.1.2, on rhadamanth (macOS, the Hammerspoon engine). main at 69171b43 carries arngz 1.1.3.

`arngz apply` reports an entry `failed` when the window reached the origin it was given but the app would not take the size. Some apps fix their window size and cannot fill the cells a desk gives them, so the desk is as well arranged as it can be and apply still exits 1.

com.appgate.sdp (Appgate SDP) is the case in hv's logs. Its window is 375x667 and will not resize. `discover` recorded it snapped to 2x2 cells of an 8x4 grid, 450x545, which the app refuses, so every apply of a desk holding it fails. The origin agrees and only the size differs:

```text
setFrame returned, and the window took 900,40 375x667, not 900,40 450x545 (an app may fix its size or snap it)
```

Repro: `arngz apply <desk>` for any desk holding com.appgate.sdp as `discover` recorded it. The entry is reported `failed` and apply exits 1, with every other entry placed.

## Measured

Read first-hand by utilz-vc at main's head 69171b43, and from hv's `~/.local/state/menuz/menuz.log` (1126 lines, runs 1 to 70, 2026-10-16T19:10:59Z to 2026-11-10T05:19:53Z).

- `opt/arngz/lib/arngz.lua:398` to `:408`: after `setFrame` the engine sleeps 150 ms, reads the frame back, and returns `status = "done"` only when `P.frames_agree(got, op.frame)`. Any disagreement, of origin or of size, falls through to `status = "failed"` with the reason quoted above. There is no case for a window that reached its origin at a size the app enforces.
- Every run in the log with its exit, counted **by command rather than by label**: of the 33 runs whose command is `arngz apply "$MENUZ_ITEM"`, **29 exited 1, 4 exited 2, and not one has ever exited 0.** Counting by command matters: the log's 7 exit-0 non-Discover runs are `Empty the Trash` and six `utilz macoz bg` items, not applies, and reading them as applies is how this looks like a 7-in-40 problem rather than a 0-in-33 one.
- com.appgate.sdp is the most frequent failed entry in the whole log: **15**, last at run 70 (2026-11-10T05:19:53Z). In **10** of those runs it was the only failed or skipped entry, so it alone decided the exit: runs 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 42, 56, 61, 62, 67.
- Run 70 is the sharpest case. Run 69 (`Discover…`, 05:19:19Z) saved zeophq from the screens present and exited 0; run 70, a `Desks…` apply of that same desk on those same screens 20 s later, exited 1, its only failures being Appgate and Notion. **A desk `discover` has just saved does not apply cleanly.** That is the test that separates a real defect from the environment.
- Measured and **not** this issue: 8 exit-1 runs (38, 43, 45, 46, 49, 50, 53, 63) carry no failed and no skipped entry at all. That is issue 0132, fixed on main by efdd047d and unreleased.

Why it matters: 0132's fix removes those 8 runs, and `apply` will still never exit 0, because this is the next cause in line. 0132's own reason for being was that nothing which runs arngz, menuz's Desks menu included, can tell a desk applied from one that broke. That remains true after 0132 ships, and this issue is why.

A note on severity, hv's to settle: filed `medium` to match 0132, which is the same class of defect. The case for `high` is that it is the single reason `apply` has a 0-for-33 record and will keep one after 0132 ships.

## Fix

utilz-vc's recommendation: `apply` counts a window that reached its cells' origin, at a size the app enforces, as **placed**, and says so in its report rather than silently, eg `placed at the app's own size, 375x667`. The engine already holds the readback at `arngz.lua:400`, so the test is that the origin agrees and the size does not. Reporting it matters: a window that is smaller than its cells is worth seeing, it just is not a failure.

Alternatives, each hv's to pick instead:

1. `discover` records such a window by origin only, leaving its size to the app. A desk-format change, M.
2. A never-record list naming the bundles that fix their size. XS to write, but a list to maintain, and Molt-matts 9adb5ae ("arngz: drop Appgate from every desk", 2 Nov) shows the failure mode: every later `discover` re-records it, which has already happened twice on homere and once on zeophq.

Not in this fix, each hv's to ask for separately:

- Notion's refusal in run 70 has a different cause and is filed as its own issue: `discover` recorded it clamped into the edge cell.
- `create_space` / `addSpaceToScreen returned nil` ("unable to get Mission Control data from the Dock"): 7 failed entries, confined to runs 32 and 35, both of which failed for several other reasons as well, so it decided no run's exit on its own. A watch item, not filed.
- The pointer-taken-back, full-screen-space-between-desktops, AXWebArea-title-bar and launched-with-no-window-in-time causes in runs 32, 39, 40, 44, 51, 58, 59, 60 and 64: by design or environmental on the reading so far.

With this issue, 0132 and the clamp issue all fixed, 19 of the 29 exit-1 runs in the log would have been clean: the 8 of 0132, the 10 of this one, and run 70 which needs this one and the clamp both.

Size S. Owner Utilz, scheduled by hv.

**Sequencing, binding.** 2.14.9's release runs (R1, R2, R3 and the tree-scan files) are all pinned on 195b1c91, and the cut's own precondition is that nothing outside `intent/` has moved since that sha. This fix lands outside `intent/`, so it must not land on main before hv's cut of 2.14.9, or every one of those runs is void and has to be run again. Cut first, or build in a worktree and merge after.

hv's standing word on 10 Nov is analysis only, with AE's 0.3.x taking total focus and no brew release, so the design goes in this issue before any source edit. Meanwhile `utilz use dev` puts arngz 1.1.3 live and so retires 0132's 8 runs with no new code and no change to the tree.

## Design

utilz-vc, 10 Nov 2026, ST0032/01, each file:line read at main's head 35025ba0. Size: S.

The decision this issue is about, whether a readback counts as placed, is domain logic: a decision, which `IN-AG-PFIC-001` puts in the pure core, not in the boundary adapter. Today it sits in `exec_place` (`arngz.lua:387` to `:408`), inside the engine, which loads only under Hammerspoon and which therefore **no suite covers**: `plan_test.lua` runs under plain Lua and `arngz.bats` drives the shim. That is why the fix moves the decision into `plan.lua` rather than adding a third branch where it stands. It is the same reasoning 0132's amended design used to give the unseen rule one home.

1. **A pure predicate for the origin.** Beside `P.frames_agree` (`plan.lua:58`), add `P.origins_agree(a, b, slack)`, the same slack arithmetic over `x` and `y` only, defaulting to `P.FRAME_SLACK` (`plan.lua:24`, 2). It does not copy the arithmetic: `P.frames_agree` is rewritten as `P.origins_agree(a, b, slack) and P.sizes_agree(a, b, slack)`, so the slack rule keeps one home (`IN-AG-HIGHLANDER-001`) and the three predicates cannot drift apart.

2. **A pure outcome function.** Add `P.place_outcome(got, want, slack)` in `plan.lua`, returning one of three strings and nothing else:
   - `"placed"` when `P.frames_agree(got, want)`, as today;
   - `"own_size"` when `P.origins_agree(got, want)` and the sizes do not agree: the window is where the desk put it, at a size the app enforces;
   - `"failed"` when the origin does not agree, or `got` is nil.

   The order matters and is asserted: a window whose origin is wrong is `failed` whatever its size, because a window in the wrong place is a real failure, which is the one thing this change must not swallow.

3. **`exec_place` becomes a thin coordinator** (`IN-AG-THIN-COORD-001`): it does its Hammerspoon work as now, then reads `P.place_outcome(got, op.frame)` and maps it:
   - `"placed"` -> `{ status = "done", readback = { frame = got } }`, unchanged;
   - `"own_size"` -> `{ status = "done", readback = { frame = got }, note = string.format("placed at the app's own size, %sx%s", P.round(got.w), P.round(got.h)) }`;
   - `"failed"` -> today's `failed` result with today's reason, verbatim, so a genuine misplacement reads exactly as it does now.

   No branch is added to the engine beyond that mapping, and the wording of the existing failure does not change.

4. **The report says so.** `P.apply_report` (`plan.lua:993`) today appends a `why` only for results that are not `done`, so a note on a `done` result would be silently dropped. It gains one addition: a `done` result carrying `note` contributes it to a `notes` list for that entry, and the line becomes `<name> (<path>): <outcome> (<notes>)` when there are notes and is byte-identical to today's when there are none. An entry with a note still counts as placed, so `code` is untouched by it. This is deliberately not folded into `why`: `why` is the account of something that went wrong, and merging the two would make a placed entry read as a failure to anything parsing the line.

5. **Tests, red at the base and green at the fix**, all pure and runnable under plain Lua, which is what makes this change provable at all given the engine is uncovered:
   - `plan_test.lua`: `P.origins_agree` agrees on a shared origin with differing sizes and disagrees past the slack on `x` and on `y`; `P.frames_agree` keeps every answer it gives today, which is the regression guard on splitting it;
   - `plan_test.lua`: `P.place_outcome` returns `own_size` for Appgate's actual numbers, `got = 900,40 375x667` against `want = 900,40 450x545`, taken from hv's log rather than invented; `placed` when the frames agree; `failed` when only the size agrees but the origin is 1920 off, which is issue 0134's case and must stay a failure here; `failed` for a nil `got`;
   - `plan_test.lua`: `P.apply_report` renders the note on a placed entry and exits 0, and renders a placed entry with no note byte-identical to today;
   - `plan_test.lua`: an entry with a note beside a genuinely failed entry still exits 1, so a note cannot mask a failure.

   The expected count is not written down by hand anywhere: each check asserts its own outcome, per the project's no-magic-numbers rule.

6. **What no suite runs, and how it is proved.** `exec_place`'s own lines load only inside Hammerspoon. Its change is the three-way mapping in step 3 and nothing else, so vc reads those bytes directly, and the behaviour they stand on is proved pure in step 5. The live proof is hv's own case: `arngz apply zeophq` on the zeophq screens reporting Appgate `placed (placed at the app's own size, 375x667)` and exiting 0, which is also WP01's acceptance test.

7. **Docs.** `help/arngz.md`: apply's report paragraph gains the `own_size` note and says an app that fixes its own window size is placed, not failed; the Exit Status `1` bullet is unchanged, since nothing new exits 1. The CHANGELOG's `[2.14.9] - unreleased` gains a Fixed entry. arngz's own version is hv's to set: vc's reading is that this release makes it 1.2.0 rather than 1.1.4, since ST0032/04 adds two verbs to the same release, and hv has ruled the Utilz release number stays the patch 2.14.9 regardless.

8. **Runs.** None that this session may start: vc decision 74 stands, and the desk is agentic-engineering-vc's. The arms above are `plan_test.lua` under plain Lua, which is the smallest run that proves the change (vc decision 67), plus `arngz.bats`'s existing apply and report tests as the regression guard. They need hv's own run or a desk grant.

## The proof standard, as measured afterwards

utilz-vc, 10 Nov 2026, recorded here because step 6 above offers "vc reads those bytes directly" as this change's proof and the next reader deserves to know how that went.

**It held here.** `exec_place`'s change had **four readings by three readers and no defect found**: critic-lua read it, utilz-dc read it going at it specifically, and the only hazard chased was whether `P.round` existed for the own-size note, which it does (`plan.lua:31`).

**It failed three times in the same thread, on the same day, under the same words**, in issue 0135's `exec_create_space`: three commits, a defect found after each, every one by a reader rather than by the reading. The two functions differ in a way that predicts it. This change is a stateless mapping — call a pure function, branch three ways, return — with no loop, no mutable state and no ordering between an effect and a read, so there is nothing to hold in your head while reading it. `exec_create_space` has a retry loop, two captured mutable locals, run-scoped state outliving the call, and an ordering dependency between an effect that creates something and a read known to lag behind it.

So "read it in the bytes" is not disproved by this thread and is not vindicated by it either. It is bounded: sound for a stateless mapping, insufficient where there is state, an effect, and an order between them. ST0032's `design.md` carries the full measurement and the open question it feeds, which is hv's. The distinction is utilz-dc's, after it corrected its own first account.
